title: What are you doing at the weekend?

sections.title: Mit csinálsz?
sections.content: *Csinál* means to do or to make, so *Mit csinálsz?* asks "What are you doing?". Add a day to ask about a plan: *Mit csinálsz szombaton?* (the day takes *-on*; *vasárnap* takes no ending). Answer with what you know: an infinitive and *megy* for a plan (*Kirándulni megyek.*), *szeretnék* and an infinitive for a wish (*Moziba szeretnék menni.*), or a plain verb for something certain (*Este filmet nézek.*).

sections.title: Ask and answer
rows: What are you doing on Saturday?
On Saturday I am going hiking.
What are you doing on Sunday?
On Sunday I would like to go to the cinema.
In the evening I watch a film.

items.english: What are you doing on Saturday?
On Saturday I am going hiking.
On Sunday we are going to the cinema.
In the evening I am watching a film.
In the afternoon I would like to swim.

sections.content: Answer *Mit csinálsz?* with the activity itself: *Úszni megyek.* There is no need to repeat *csinál*. Keep *vasárnap* and *este* bare, but add *-on* to *szombat*: *szombaton*.
